name: TLC272CDR
title: Dual precision CMOS operational amplifier, 3 V to 16 V single supply
summary: TLC272, TLC272A, TLC272B and TLC277 are dual CMOS op amps with picoamp input bias current and inputs whose common-mode range reaches just below the negative rail; the output also swings to that rail. The four grades step offset down from 10 mV to 500 µV maximum. C-suffix parts run from 3 V to 16 V over 0 °C to 70 °C and I-suffix parts from 4 V to 16 V over –40 °C to 85 °C. TLC272CDR is the TLC272 C grade in an SOIC-8 on tape and reel.

circuits.title: State-variable filter
circuits.description: Three amplifiers form a state-variable filter that gives high-pass, band-pass and low-pass outputs at once from one input. The first amplifier sums the input, the low-pass output and, through its non-inverting input, a share of the band-pass output; its output is the high-pass signal. The second and third amplifiers are integrators (10 kΩ into 0.016 µF), giving band-pass and then low-pass. The resistor R from the band-pass output to the 5 kΩ divider sets the damping d = 1/Q. The circuit runs from a single 5 V supply.
notes: The 5 V supply and ground are common to all three amplifiers.
The second amplifier of U2 is not part of the filter.

circuits.title: Inverting amplifier with voltage reference
circuits.description: A single-supply inverting amplifier whose non-inverting input sits at a reference VREF made by dividing VDD with R1 and R3; C, 0.01 µF, filters the reference. The input VI drives the inverting node through R2 and R4 sets the gain, so the output swings about VREF by –R4/R2 times the difference VI – VREF.

circuits.title: Unity-gain amplifier test circuit, single supply
circuits.description: Voltage follower used for measurements on one supply: the output feeds the inverting input directly, and the load RL and CL return to ground.

circuits.title: Unity-gain amplifier test circuit, split supply
circuits.description: The same follower on split supplies; the load RL and CL return to the negative rail VDD–, so the result matches the single-supply circuit.

circuits.title: Noise test circuit, single supply
circuits.description: Stage for input noise measurement: each input sees 20 Ω to a mid-supply bias of half VDD, and 2 kΩ feeds the output back to the inverting input.

circuits.title: Noise test circuit, split supply
circuits.description: The noise stage on split supplies: each input sees 20 Ω to ground, with 2 kΩ from the output to the inverting input.

circuits.title: Gain-of-100 inverting amplifier test circuit, single supply
circuits.description: Inverting stage with 100 Ω in and 10 kΩ feedback; the non-inverting input is held at half VDD and the load capacitor CL returns to ground.

circuits.title: Gain-of-100 inverting amplifier test circuit, split supply
circuits.description: The gain-of-100 stage on split supplies: the non-inverting input is grounded and CL returns to the negative rail VDD–.

operation.text: Two independent CMOS op amps per package. Four grades differ in input offset: TLC272 (10 mV maximum at 25 °C), TLC272A (5 mV), TLC272B (2 mV) and TLC277 (500 µV). The C suffix is rated 0 °C to 70 °C with a 3 V to 16 V supply; the I suffix –40 °C to 85 °C with 4 V to 16 V. Input impedance is typically above 10^12 Ω and the parts carry ESD protection and built-in latch-up immunity. TLC272CDR is the TLC272 C-suffix grade in SOIC-8 on a 2500-piece reel, marked 272C.

The amplifiers are built for one supply: the input common-mode range takes in ground and the output pulls down to ground. C-suffix parts work from 3 V, which covers TTL and HCMOS logic rails; the widest signal range comes from a 16 V single supply. Split supplies work as well. To bias an input above ground a resistive divider is enough, and the low bias current allows very high divider values and so little divider current.

When linear parts and digital logic share a power supply, feed the amplifiers from their own bypassed supply lines rather than from the rails the logic switches on, since the logic's current spikes move those rails. A single decoupling capacitor usually serves; at high frequency an RC decoupling network may be needed.

Going past the specified input range on either input can make the part misbehave. The lower limit includes the negative rail; the upper limit is VDD – 1 V at 25 °C and VDD – 1.5 V across the rest of the temperature range.

A polysilicon-gate CMOS process holds threshold shifts, and so offset drift, well below those of metal-gate CMOS: the dopant that causes the shift sits in a conductor instead of the oxide. Long-term offset drift is calculated at typically 0.1 µV per month, the first month included.

Board and socket leakage can easily exceed the input bias current. Guard rings round the inputs help; each guard is driven from a low-impedance point at the common-mode input voltage. In a non-inverting stage the guard ties to the feedback node at the inverting input, in an inverting stage to the grounded non-inverting input, and in a follower to the output.
An amplifier left unused is wired as a unity-gain follower with its input grounded, so that it cannot oscillate.
With so little input bias current the noise current is negligible in most circuits, an advantage over bipolar inputs once source and circuit impedances exceed 50 kΩ.
An output may be shorted to either supply without a time limit at 25 °C or below, provided temperature and supply keep dissipation inside the package rating.

At room temperature the bias current is typically under 1 pA, below the leakage of a test socket. Two ways to measure it: surround the inputs with grounded shield metal (on JG and P packages the isolation metal runs between and round the input pins), and read the open socket first and subtract that from the reading with the part in place. Testers that infer bias current from the drop across a series input resistor cannot take an open-socket reading.
The low-level output depends on both the common-mode input level and the differential input voltage, so both must match the specified conditions when comparing a measurement to the VOL figures.

The coefficient is calculated from offset readings at two temperatures. Below freezing, moisture on the part and socket causes leakage and contact resistance that corrupt the offset reading, and the guard metal is covered too, so measurements are best made above 0 °C.
The typical-characteristics graphs are given at TA = 25 °C, VS = ±20 V, VCM = VS/2, RLOAD = 10 kΩ to VS/2 and CL = 10 pF unless a graph states otherwise.
